what_this_is: The scanner's fallback counter is a heuristic: one token per CJK codepoint, one per four other characters. This file records how far off that heuristic actually is, measured rather than assumed.
Factors are heuristic_tokens / real_tokens. To correct a heuristic count, DIVIDE by the factor.
A factor below 1.0 means the heuristic undercounts.

method.sample: 414 files drawn from the elmos corpus, stratified by extension proportionally to file count, seed 20260819

reference_tokenizer.name: legacy Claude BPE tokenizer
reference_tokenizer.obtained_from: anthropic==0.21.3, anthropic/tokenizer.json (the last release that bundled it)
reference_tokenizer.caveat: This is NOT the tokenizer of any current model. It is a real BPE tokenizer of the right family and rough vocabulary scale, which makes it a far better yardstick than the 4-characters-per-token rule -- but it is a yardstick, not ground truth. Billing-grade counts still require the target provider's own counting endpoint.

excluded_from_by_extension: Every other extension in the sample had fewer than 5 files or fewer than 5000 real tokens. Their observed factors ranged from 0.52 to 1.13, which on one file is noise, not a measurement. They fall back to the global factor.
reading_the_numbers: Structured data is where the heuristic is worst: YAML 0.60 and JSON 0.75. Punctuation-dense text tokenises into many short tokens, and the four-characters rule cannot see that.
Prose and mainstream code are close to right: Markdown 1.02, Python 1.02, Java 1.08.
So a repository's error depends on its file mix. Re-measure after the mix changes materially.
